verdicts.why: The only new stage is MIT, where Riri is a student. Student stages are not counted for now, and without it the proposal is the same as the current record (Hood's Crew, then Independent, both in Ironheart).

The Columbia University stage is dropped because he is a student there. Joe's Pizza holds up: Mr. Aziz cites 'Joe's 29-minute guarantee' and fires Peter in the first scene of SM2, while he keeps freelancing for the Bugle, so the Bugle is re-entered as his last stage.

On screen, Eddie signs off with 'I'm Eddie Brock, and this is The Brock Report' (his boss also calls it 'the Eddie Brock show'). I found nothing that shows the name 'The Eddie Brock Report', and the network's name (MNBN) is never said. He is fired, and at the end he turns down the network's offer to bring the show back.
This is the twin of Eddie Brock (Sony), so it mirrors item 2002. The show's on-screen name is 'The Brock Report', not 'The Eddie Brock Report'.

The opening shot shows the band's name, 'The Mary Janes', on Gwen's bass drum. She quits early in the film ('How's the band?' / 'I quit'), then joins Miguel's Spider-Society and later leaves it. The stages are in story order.

Her studies alone would not count, but in S2E13 she wins the post of Dr. Connors's lab assistant and works in ESU's neogenic lab, which counts as working at a school. ESU is named in the show ('Empire State', S1E1). She is never shown leaving. The owner may still treat a student assistantship as part of her studies.
Midtown High is the only stage, and MJ is a student there. Student stages are not counted for now, so the record stays Independent.
Both stages are high schools Nico attends as a student (Midtown, then Rockford T. Bales). Student stages are not counted for now, so the record stays Independent.

In Hawkeye ep 2 Kate works at her mother's firm: 'Not showing up at work is not safe', 'She owns a security company', and Eleanor says 'If it's for work, I'm your boss' and 'in the fall you'll start working at Bishop Security for real'. Eleanor's arrest doesn't close the firm (an unsure case keeps the group), and Kate moves when she joins the Young Avengers in The Marvels.

In Runaways S3E6 she is already working at Wizard ('She's working at Wizard?'), and Robert names her 'the new CEO of Wizard'. Later in the same episode her coven inducts Nico ('your initiation into our coven'), and she leads it to the end; banishment is not a departure. The proposal uses the existing names 'Wizard' and 'Morgan's coven', as already reconciled in audit2 STATE.

The recreated Flint is enrolled at Coulson Academy as a student, which isn't counted. Izel possesses him once, against his will, to rebuild the monoliths: he is her victim, not a member serving a crew, and the screen never names any 'Izel's Crew'. Nothing remains, so Independent stands.

The Midtown and MIT stages are dropped because she is a student at both. In Brand New Day she has spent four years at MIT, graduated and moved back. She has just turned down a job ('I got the job... I turned it down... I don't wanna work for some soulless corporation'), so she stands with no group. This also settles the open owner call about the donut shop.
In She-Hulk ep 4-5 the papers are 'filed by Titania Worldwide LLC', and her She-Hulk by Titania product line is sold through it. Losing the case doesn't end the company.

He coaches wrestling at the community center (said in S3E5-6: 'a wrestling coach at a community center', 'a volunteer for the community center'). The gym banners in his S3E7 class read 'Willie Dance Community Center'. Arrest and death are not moves.

Selby runs the bar ('People don't just come into my bar'), but the name 'Brass Monkey Saloon' is never said in the episode. Its sign is a wordless monkey-head neon, and the name comes from tie-in material (the Explore Madripoor site). With no on-screen name the stage fails.

Jarvis says 'Welcome to Stark Pictures'. Agatha is the studio's star on Cosmic Queen, offers Kingo 'a three-picture deal' on Howard's behalf, and ends planning the sequel with Stark. The owner may weigh her as a one-film hire, but she works inside the studio throughout.

The S1E2 'death' is rightly not a move. In S2E2 the brainwashed Morph fights alongside Ruckus and Hairbag for Sinister, and in S2E12-13 alongside George, Ruckus and Vertigo; the show names this crew 'the Nasty Boys' in S4E8. He returns in S4E3 ('Morph's homecoming') and leaves in S4E12. One change from the proposal: he is back with the team in the TAS finale (S5E14: 'Morph, it is nice to see you home... truly an X-Man'), so his last X-Men stage belongs to the animated series, not X-Men '97.

No transcript was available, and the sources disagree on the cult's name: the Marvel Database says 'Center for Reunification', a review says 'Church of Reunification'. I could not confirm that either name is said or shown on screen, so the stage fails. An owner call is possible: MJ's brainwashed service to Mordo's cult would count if the name is confirmed.
